_doc: Low-voltage pathways (Q6203 lvpathways): how each low-voltage outlet's pathway is read from the documents and routed when they say nothing. Words are how statements are recognised (the documents' own statements always win); defaults are company defaults, each with its source.

kinds.source: a low-voltage outlet is a device whose kind names a communications, security or audio-visual outlet (TIA-568 work area outlets, card readers, cameras, access points); fire alarm devices have their own wiring

methods.prefer_source: company default: where the documents allow more than one method ("conduit or ENT"), the first of these they allow, the lighter and quicker one to install; a method the documents name alone is used as named

one_per_room: EACH GUEST ROOM SHALL HAVE ONE

concealed: CONCEALED IN CEILINGS AND INTERIOR WALLS
exposed: EXPOSED, NOT SUBJECT TO PHYSICAL DAMAGE
EXPOSED, NOT SUBJECT TO SEVERE PHYSICAL DAMAGE

statements.source: a document statement of a low-voltage pathway: a note, legend note or specification paragraph naming a pathway (conduit, tubing, stub, sleeve, J-hooks) for low-voltage outlets; the low-voltage system's own documents (its sheets, Division 27 and 28) govern its pathways over a general electrical note, a more specific statement (a kind of outlet, a type of room) over a general one

unit.source: rules default: a dwelling or guest unit's low-voltage outlet gets 3/4" ENT from its box up the wall and over the room's ceiling into the corridor's ceiling space, where the cabling runs (NEC 362.10 allows ENT concealed in walls, floors and ceilings; TIA-569 work area pathway)

common.source: rules default: an outlet outside the units gets a 3/4" EMT stub from its box up into the accessible ceiling space above (TIA-569 work area pathway; NEC 358.10)

exposed.source: rules default: an outlet in an exposed room (mechanical, electrical, storage) gets a 3/4" EMT stub up to the structure (NEC 358.10)

geometry.source: company default: a stub ends 6 in above the ceiling it rises into; a run to the corridor ends 1 ft past the corridor's wall in its ceiling space; a device within 6 in of its ceiling is in the ceiling space already (its cable needs no raceway to reach it)

fittings.stub_end_source: NEC 300.4(G) and the usual communications pathway specification: a stub-up not ending in a box or enclosure ends in an insulated bushing (protects the cable)
fittings.pull_string_source: TIA-569 and the usual communications pathway specification: a pull line in every empty pathway, its length the pathway's plus 2 ft at each end

bracket.source: rules default: a low-voltage outlet takes a box (the device box the build makes) unless the documents call for a low-voltage bracket or mud ring at it

jhooks.spacing_source: TIA-569 / BICSI: a cable support at most every 5 ft and at each change of direction
jhooks.ours_source: rules default: J-hooks and open cable are the cabling contractor's (they are not a raceway); a document putting them on the electrical trade makes them ours

sleeve.source: TIA-569 / IBC 714: a cable pathway through a rated wall passes in a sleeve one trade size over the pathway, firestopped with a listed system

firestop.source: IBC 714 / NEC 300.21 and 800.26: penetrations of fire-rated walls and floors by low-voltage pathways firestopped with a listed system; the rating is the crossed wall type's assembly (partition legend)
firestop.ours_source: rules default: the trade that makes the penetration firestops it, unless the documents give it to another
